statement: In Java a binary tree is usually stored as linked objects: a TreeNode class with an int val and two references, left and right, which are null when that child is absent.

You are given the values of a tree as the array tree in level order, indexed from 0. The left and right children of the value at index i are at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2, and null marks a position with no node.

Turn the array into linked TreeNode objects. Create the root from tree[0]; for every later non-null value, create a node and attach it as the left child (odd index) or right child (even index) of the node at index (i − 1) / 2. A value whose parent position never got a node has nothing to attach to, so it is not part of the tree.
Return the number of TreeNode objects that end up linked into the tree.

examples.explanation: Index 3 is null, so 2 has no left child. 4 becomes 2's right child, and 5 and 6 become the children of 3. All six values are linked.
Index 2 is null, so no node exists there. 5 and 4, at indices 5 and 6, would be its children, but they have no parent to attach to. Only 9, 8, 7 and 6 are linked.
